answer: One workable design: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because pulse only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any umber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
